Theorems~2.3 and~3.1 show local nonuniform impossibility for estimating post-model-selection distributions in broad nested and AIC-like selection problems.
Theorem~3 derives a local focused-selection law and Theorem~4 guarantees coverage at least \(1-\alpha-\gamma\) for a fixed invalid-instrument selection problem.
Theorem~3.1 characterizes ordinary-bootstrap validity by full differentiability under a Gaussian limit, and Theorem~3.2 validates derivative-aware resampling.
The sorting operator is Hadamard differentiable at regular values and yields a uniform sorted-process central limit theorem and bootstrap bands on compact interior quantile sets.
Theorems~2.1 and~2.6 give Gaussian and multiplier-bootstrap approximations for maxima of high-dimensional sample-mean vectors under sub-exponential or polynomial moments.
Theorem~1 gives selective coverage by simultaneous inference over a data-dependent set of locally plausible targets.
Conditional truncated-Gaussian and hybrid projection procedures correct the winner's curse when a target coordinate is selected by optimizing noisy estimates.
Theorem~2.3 gives exact Fisher-randomization-test size under a sharp null, and Theorem~3.5 gives an excess-risk bound for an adaptive conformal borrowing threshold.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Derive from primitive score-index regularity the corrected all-prefix estimator and criterion process for the actual generated fixed-cardinality path, then prove direct or anti-concentrated localization and the selected-estimator law across fixed, vanishing, and exact gaps.
open_obligations.obstruction: The named smooth-localizable attempt still lacks differentiability of the map that integrates a score-dependent summand over a fitted-score sublevel set.  Finite-dimensional pointwise score smoothness, a one-dimensional density bound, and Hölder score-indexed moments do not imply that derivative.  Without it there are no corrected resampling summands, and the subsequent coercive-well and anti-concentration localization argument has no valid input process.
open_obligations.attempted: On the explicitly named smooth-localizable generated-prefix class \(\mathcal P^{\mathrm{SL}}\), the displayed estimator was decomposed into a fixed-threshold empirical process, an external empirical-quantile boundary term, and a fitted-score boundary perturbation.  The quantile term linearizes under the density and Hölder trace conditions.  The fitted-score difference quotient need not converge: a Lipschitz boundary trace can have directional cusps, and a Hölder exponent below one can magnify a root-\(n\) score perturbation.  The process gate therefore fails before fixed-, vanishing-, or exact-gap near-minimizer transfer can be proved.

prose_updates.tldr: Influence-ranked external-control borrowing has two verified necessity boundaries inside the displayed Yang--Li--Wu--Yang sample architecture.  A continuous generated ranking can create a quantitatively nondegenerate, non-Gaussian fixed-cardinality boundary term, so the frozen \(\Gamma_n\)-Gaussian all-prefix coupling and every covariance-only repair fail.  Separately, exact leading-risk ties can retain nonvanishing root-\(n\) ATE-coordinate distance, including between two positive prefixes; the repaired finite-support witness also defines the external potential outcomes on every row.  No Yang theorem asserts the refuted coupling.  A bounded feasibility attempt on a smooth-localizable generated-prefix subclass fails at the primitive fitted-score sublevel-set derivative, so the corrected selected law, sharp observable modulus, and computable tie-uniform interval remain unresolved and the present negative-plus-conditional package does not meet the positive Stat field-tier inference floor.

project_justification.gap: Yang, Li, Wu, and Yang's equations~(2)--(3) and Algorithm~1 define the squared outcome-regression fit, generated influence ranking, and positive top-\(k\) prefixes.  Their fixed-set Theorems~1--2 do not assert a generated all-prefix coupling, and their Theorem~3 assumes a fixed positive MSE gap and is silent at multiple minima.  The rank-boundary-corrected process, local-gap selected law, observable modulus, and post-selection ATE interval are therefore additional problems rather than consequences of those theorems.
project_justification.niche: The verified boundary separates leading-risk proximity from proximity of the root-\(n\) ATE coordinates.  The positive-prefix theorem supplies separated-coordinate geometry at the exact zero-gap boundary excluded by Yang's Theorem~3, so any valid localization or confidence interval must pay an unavoidable width cost unless extra observable structure controls both bias and covariance.
project_justification.fill: The project proves a non-Gaussian fixed-cardinality boundary witness with an explicit positive-probability nondegeneracy event, proves separate exact-tie coordinate separation witnesses, and retains a conditional quadratic transfer lemma.  It also performs one substantive smooth-localizable-subclass feasibility attempt from the actual sample maps.  That attempt derives the required decomposition but cannot justify the fitted-score sublevel-set derivative from the proposed primitive package; consequently it establishes no corrected all-prefix process, near-minimizer law, matching observable modulus, or uniformly valid multiplier interval.

prose_updates.related_work: Yang, Li, Wu, and Yang define the squared outcome-regression empirical risk minimizer in equation~(2), its generated influence score in equation~(3), and the nested positive top-\(k\) workflow in Algorithm~1.  Their Theorems~1--2 concern a given borrowed set, while Theorem~3 assumes a given ranking and fixed positive MSE separation.  No theorem there asserts the uniform local all-prefix coupling refuted here.  The positive-prefix tie theorem supplies separated-coordinate geometry precisely at the multiple-minimum boundary on which Theorem~3 is silent.  Mogstad, Romano, Shaikh, and Wilhelm treat inference for random ranks and provide a relevance precedent for tie handling, but not selection among generated external-control prefixes.  Valancius and coauthors provide hybrid-trial sampling and positivity structure, but not generated influence ranking or local-gap selection.  Claeskens and Hjort supply the focused local-misspecification architecture.  Patel, DiTraglia, Zuber, and Burgess study focused-selector inference for a fixed invalid-instrument problem, not estimated individual ranks.  Leeb and Poetscher give the generic local nonuniformity background.  Fang and Santos motivate derivative-aware resampling at nondifferentiable maps.  Chernozhukov, Fernandez-Val, and Luo establish sorting derivatives under stronger regular-value structure, but pointwise smooth score fitting, a scalar density, and Hölder score-indexed moments alone do not deliver the fitted-score sublevel-set derivative needed here.  Gaussian, multiplier, and localization results of Chernozhukov and coauthors, Zrnic and Fithian, and Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey become applicable only after the corrected ranked functional and its anti-concentrated local set have been derived.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The continuous-score boundary witness deliberately permits score-indexed outcome behavior oscillating at the empirical quantile scale; a density margin alone cannot exclude its non-Gaussian first-order term.  The smooth-localizable feasibility attempt adds finite-dimensional smooth score fitting, an interior density bounded above and away from zero, Hölder conditional moments, uniform nuisance entropy and rates, edge-risk exclusion, finitely many coercive wells, and nondegenerate joint noise.  Even this list does not imply differentiability of the fitted-score sublevel-set integral: pointwise score smoothness does not control the boundary trace as the fitted parameter moves.  A new primitive Hadamard or surface-differentiability condition and a proof of its uniform empirical remainder are needed before localization or multiplier calibration can begin.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved negative results remain logically separate.  One regular continuous-score sequence gives a deterministic interior prefix with a non-Gaussian rank-boundary contribution, invalidating the frozen \(\Gamma_n\)-Gaussian coupling and every covariance-only Gaussian repair.  A separate regular sequence gives an exact tie between two positive prefixes with nonvanishing ATE-coordinate distance, and the fully specified finite-support legal sequence gives an independent no-borrowing tie witness.  None proves that the MSE selector chooses the non-Gaussian coordinate, so no selected marginal law is established or refuted.  The conditional transfer lemma is not achievability for the generated path, and the multiplier definition is only a proposed handle with no current computability or coverage guarantee.  The smooth-localizable attempt fails at its first corrected-process gate; accordingly the sharp excess modulus, selected law, and tie-uniform interval remain open, and the current package is not a completed field-tier Stat contribution.
